24 A siren emits sound of frequency 1000 Hz. The siren moves at 20 m s–1 towards an observer who
is standing still.
The speed of sound in the air is 330 m s–1.
Which expression would correctly give the frequency heard by the observer?

hints: Notice the wording: the $1000\text{ Hz}$ siren is the moving source at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a standing-still observer, so the waves ahead are crowded together.
Connect this to observed wavelength: in one period the source moves $v_s/f_s$, so the wavelength in front is $\lambda_o = (v-v_s)/f_s$ with $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Then use $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ to decide whether $330-20$ or $330+20$ belongs on the top or bottom of the fraction for a higher heard frequency.
walkthrough: Identify the Doppler case: source frequency $f_s = 1000\text{ Hz}$, source speed $v_s = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards observer, wave speed $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$, observer speed zero.
State the rule: motion towards compresses the waves in front, so observed wavelength $\lambda_o$ is smaller and observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ is larger than $1000\text{ Hz}$.
Find $\lambda_o$: in time $T = 1/f_s$ sound travels $vT$ but the source follows by $v_sT$, so $\lambda_o = vT - v_sT = (v - v_s)/f_s = (330 - 20)/1000$.
Substitute into $f_o = v/\lambda_o = v/[(v-v_s)/f_s] = f_s \times v/(v-v_s)$, giving $f_o = 1000 \times 330/(330-20)$ with unit $\text{Hz}$.
This higher-frequency expression with $330-20$ in the denominator matches the listed fraction. This is option B.

A.explanation: Denominator $330+20$ gives $f_o < 1000\text{ Hz}$, which is the shift for a source moving away, not towards the observer.

B.explanation: Denominator $330-20$ shortens the wavelength ahead of the approaching source, giving $f_o = 1000 \times 330/(330-20) > 1000\text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Form $1000(330+20)/330$ is for an observer moving at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a stationary source, not a moving source.

D.explanation: Form $1000(330-20)/330$ is for an observer moving at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ away from a stationary source, not a moving source.
